title: Transactional rendering and failure containment
summary: Incoming snapshots/patches are validated against a semantic mirror before any Swing mutation. Ordinary Wire/application/rendering faults are contained at property/component/subtree/patch/window scope rather than escaping through the EDT or terminating the process.
invariants: Patch preflight completes before visual commit.
Revision/view/parent/definition/order invariants are checked before Swing mutation.
A rejected structural patch retains the previously committed component tree.
Unknown/unsupported primitives produce controlled placeholders or local errors rather than process failure.
A stale or malformed patch requests resynchronisation where appropriate; it is never applied optimistically.
PROCESS scope is not used for ordinary renderer faults.
procedure: Build a proposed semantic state from the patch.
Validate exact definitions, revision continuity and structural relationships.
Marshal one bounded commit to the EDT.
On failure, retain previous committed state and emit bounded renderer evidence.
